text:
I originally got these shorts to wear around the yard when I do my yard work. We have a rather large yard so I am always gardening, weeding, and doing other work around the property. Having shorts like these seemed like a good idea.

FABRIC
The fabric of these shorts is soft and well worn. They will last a summer maybe.

STYLE
The style fits well and is actually big on me which surprised me. At least in the waist and hips I mean. The 2XL in other clothing has barely fit my kid who is a size 12, so I got the 2XL expecting them to be small. They aren't.

LENGTH
Look, I am a clothing designer and have made and designed clothing for a long time. When you have shorts that fit the way they are supposed to, the front is shorter and the back edge is supposed to be LONGER to cover the larger area of the buttocks. You are not supposed to cut them off at the same length.

These shorts are ridiculous. The front is okay, but the back exposes the rear. If that is what you want, then you will like these. I don't. I like to keep my underwear to myself.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These shorts fit well on top but the legs are cut off wrong. They expose the rear a lot. The front is okay. The only way I would wear these is with bike shorts under them. I don't see myself doing that any time soon.

MY RATING
TWO STARS. The fit on top is nice, IF they had cut off the back tapered longer than the front edge, these would look much nicer, especially in larger sizes. As they are, they are awful unless you like showing your rear. I do not.

If I have some time in the future, I will alter them into something fun, but I won't be wearing them as they are.

text:
I purchased these from Walmart.com (and from Go2site. If you love these socks, they can be as low as $5/pair so shop around).

I am and RN married to and MD. Based on YouTube review by an RN, I purchased these. We have been wearing compression socks for years.

I wanted to love these socks. Awesome patterns and colors.

They would be awesome in practice if they were made of one piece of fabric, dyed multi-colored so that mmHg compression was consistent throughout the sock.

But thats not the case. The striped and argyle socks are compromised of multiple pieces sewn together. The seams have a lot of excess fabric, nearly 1/2 high in some places. That causes higher compression wherever there is excess fabric. See the picture.

Same is true in footbed of black sock.

When I took the socks off, I had deeper indentations up and down and all around my calf. The color was more red than where just the sock fabric was. I have no edema or skin problems&just normal skin.

I showed this to my MD spouse. Response? Wow&that could cause skin breakdown because of the pressure variance.

Note Dr. Scholls black 20-30mmHg compression sock at bottom of picture.. Solid piece of fabric. Seams are less prominent/dense. Thats exactly why even these high compression socks do not cause the problems I experienced with this medium compression sock.

I contacted the company and explained my concern. Their reply?

While we appreciate your feedback, we will not be taking the advice as we have many, many more customers who love our products and this is our business to run, not yours to tell us to shut down!

I was surprised at the reply. I never suggested they shut down. As a health care provider, I was concerned for others. I did encourage them to consider stop selling the product until the problem was addressed. Thats not at all telling a business to shut down.

I suggested they use a model of their sock that doesnt have the problem. For clearly the company is capable of making socks without multiple seams with all the excess fabric on each seam: as in their rainbow sock.

At a minimum, I think they should let their customers know of the multiple pieces of fabric and untrimmed seams. I never would have purchased these had this been disclosed because the wearability outcome is completely predictable.

If the excess pressure from untrimmed seams doesnt cause any impact on your skin, then Im glad they work for you.

For me, even though the rainbow socks are ok I prefer not to do business with companies that reply to a customer concern like this company did to mine. That is why I am returning even the rainbow socks.

I took one pic of the left shoe, where (and I don't know how) someone who had them before me or the factory managed to get the white tissue paper in the toe pushed so far up that it felt as if it were crazy glued in place.  I literally couldn't get it out, so even trying to get the left boot on was out of the question.  I did manage to get the right boot on and was immediately wincing in pain from the hardness of the leather.  My foot hurt for a full 30 minutes everywhere after I managed to get it off because of the scraping of the skin that occurred trying to get the boot off.  I know it was stupid, but the boots are so pretty I had to try.  Needless to say, they are going back and I WILL NOT be repurchasing any color.
